## Introduction

In this 15-minute activity, you complete and run a *targets* pipeline
that reads the selected `HealthWellbeing` version, pools the study
correlations, and writes a summary for the report. The pipeline is
partially completed: you fill in two short gaps rather than writing it
from scratch. By the end, you should be able to trace the summary back
to its input and explain which steps *targets* reruns, and why.

Work in your MyBinder session, at the project root, after preparing
the dataset versions. If you fall behind, the catch-up step gives you
the completed pipeline so you can continue with the report.
[Prepare the dataset versions](00_preparation.qmd#preparation-versions)

## The pipeline at a glance

A *target* is one named step whose result *targets* stores and
tracks. When a target's code mentions another target by name, it
depends on that target. The pipeline's targets connect in this order:

``` text
version_file -> data_version -> dataset_file -> studies -> fit
fit, data_version -> result -> summary_file
```

`version_file`, `dataset_file`, and `summary_file` are file targets:
*targets* tracks the contents of the selection file, the pinned RDS
file, and the summary CSV. When fitting, the pipeline records the
checksum of the script that ran.

The model uses the raw Pearson correlations and study sample sizes.
*meta* transforms each correlation to Fisher's z scale and pools the
effects with a random-effects model. We use restricted maximum
likelihood (REML) to estimate between-study variance and the
Hartung–Knapp method for the 95% interval. The summary converts the
estimate and limits back to the correlation scale.

This model treats study summaries as independent and assumes their
correlations address a comparable association. Differences in
populations, measures, and sampling limit interpretation. This is a
worked example of pooling reported effects from the supplied studies
[@harrer2021, sec. 4.2.4].

## Step 1: copy the workbook pipeline

Allow about two minutes. Run this in the **R Console**. It loads the
*targets* functions and copies the partially completed template to
`workspace/_targets.R`, your own working copy. The copy is only made
if it does not exist yet, so rerunning the chunk keeps your edits.
Git ignores the `workspace/` folder, so the supplied template stays
unchanged.

```{r health-targets-setup, include = TRUE, echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, cache = FALSE, output = TRUE, eval = TRUE}
box::use(
  targets[tar_make, tar_outdated, tar_read, tar_visnetwork]
)
invisible(loadNamespace("visNetwork"))

workshop_dir <- file.path("outputs", "health-wellbeing")
pipeline_template <- file.path(
  "pipelines", "exercise", "_targets_health_wellbeing.R"
)
pipeline_script <- file.path("workspace", "_targets.R")
pipeline_store <- file.path(workshop_dir, "_targets")

dir.create("workspace", showWarnings = FALSE)
if (!file.exists(pipeline_script)) {
  file.copy(pipeline_template, pipeline_script)
}
readLines(file.path(workshop_dir, "analysis-data-version.txt"))
```

The last line shows the selected dataset version. It should match the
`all` version from your preparation step.

## Step 2: run the pipeline before completing it

Allow about three minutes. Open `workspace/_targets.R` in RStudio and
read its seven numbered targets. Then draw the dependency graph and
try to run the pipeline.

```{r health-targets-first-run, include = TRUE, echo = TRUE, eval = FALSE}
tar_visnetwork(
  script = pipeline_script,
  store = pipeline_store,
  targets_only = TRUE,
  outdated = FALSE
)
tar_make(script = pipeline_script, store = pipeline_store)
```

Two arrows are missing from the graph: nothing connects `studies` to
`fit`, or `result` to `summary_file`. The run stops with the message
`Complete TODO 1 in the fit target.` *targets* found nothing to link
those steps because their code does not yet mention the targets they
need.

## Step 3: complete the two gaps

Allow about four minutes. Edit `workspace/_targets.R` and save it.

-   **TODO 1**, in step 5: replace `stop(...)` in `data = stop(...)`
    with the name of the target that holds the checked study
    summaries.
-   **TODO 2**, in step 7: replace the `stop(...)` line with two lines
    that write `result` to `path` and then return `path`.

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Solution to TODO 1

``` r
      data = studies,
```

Mentioning `studies` makes `fit` depend on it, so the graph gains an
arrow from `studies` to `fit`.
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Solution to TODO 2

``` r
      utils::write.csv(result, path, row.names = FALSE)
      path
```

A file target returns the path of the file it wrote. *targets* then
tracks the file's contents and rebuilds it if the file changes.
:::

If you are stuck, run this catch-up step. It replaces your copy with
the completed reference pipeline only while a `stop()` placeholder
remains, so it leaves a completed copy unchanged.

```{r health-targets-catch-up, include = TRUE, echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, cache = FALSE, output = TRUE, eval = TRUE}
if (any(grepl("Complete TODO", readLines(pipeline_script)))) {
  file.copy(
    file.path("pipelines", "_targets_health_wellbeing.R"),
    pipeline_script,
    overwrite = TRUE
  )
}
```

## Step 4: inspect the graph and run the pipeline

Allow about four minutes. Draw the graph again. Both missing arrows
should now appear. If you're using the PDF, follow the text diagram
above.

```{r health-targets-graph, include = TRUE, echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, cache = FALSE, output = TRUE, eval = knitr::is_html_output()}
tar_visnetwork(
  script = pipeline_script,
  store = pipeline_store,
  targets_only = TRUE,
  outdated = FALSE
)
```

Run the pipeline and read the result.

```{r health-targets-run, include = TRUE, echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, cache = FALSE, output = TRUE, eval = TRUE}
tar_make(script = pipeline_script, store = pipeline_store)
tar_read(result, store = pipeline_store)
```

On your first complete run, each target reports that it completed.
*targets* saves every result in the pipeline store, here
`outputs/health-wellbeing/_targets`, and `tar_read()` loads a saved
result without rerunning anything.

## Step 5: run it again

Allow about one minute. Run the pipeline a second time and ask which
targets are outdated.

```{r health-targets-rerun, include = TRUE, echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, cache = FALSE, output = TRUE, eval = TRUE}
tar_make(script = pipeline_script, store = pipeline_store)
tar_outdated(script = pipeline_script, store = pipeline_store)
```

Nothing runs, and no target is outdated. *targets* reruns a step only
when its code, its upstream targets, or its tracked files change.

## Checkpoint {#targets-checkpoint}

The full example combines **29 studies** with a pooled correlation of
about **0.36** and a 95% interval of about **0.31 to 0.41**. The file
`outputs/health-wellbeing/meta-summary.csv` contains the same values,
the dataset version, the method names, the R and *meta* versions, and
the checksum of your pipeline script. A second run skips every target.

Next, you will write a report that reads this summary.
[Create and render a reproducible Quarto report](06_quarto.qmd)
